question:
(a) In a class of 100 students, 35 offer History, 43 offer Geography and 50 offer Economics. 14 students offer History and Geography, 13 offer Geography and Economics and 11 offer History and Economics. The number of students that offer none of the subjects is four times the number of those that offer three subjects.
(i) How many students offer three subjects?
(ii) How many students offer none?
(iii) How many students offer only one of the subjects?
(iv) How many students offer History and Geography only?
modelAnswer:
Let x = number who offer all three subjects (H ∩ G ∩ E).
Let n = number who offer none. Given: n = 4x.

Using inclusion-exclusion:
|H ∪ G ∪ E| = |H| + |G| + |E| − |H∩G| − |G∩E| − |H∩E| + |H∩G∩E|
= 35 + 43 + 50 − 14 − 13 − 11 + x
= 90 + x

Total: |H ∪ G ∪ E| + n = 100
(90 + x) + 4x = 100
90 + 5x = 100
5x = 10
x = 2

(i) Number who offer all three subjects = 2

(ii) Number who offer none = 4x = 4 × 2 = 8

(iii) Number who offer only one subject:
|H∩G only| = 14 − 2 = 12
|G∩E only| = 13 − 2 = 11
|H∩E only| = 11 − 2 = 9

Only H = 35 − 12 − 9 − 2 = 12
Only G = 43 − 12 − 11 − 2 = 18
Only E = 50 − 11 − 9 − 2 = 28

Number offering only one subject = 12 + 18 + 28 = 58

(iv) Number offering History and Geography only = 12

question: (a) Prove by mathematical induction or otherwise that ∑_{k=1}^{n} k² = n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6.
modelAnswer:
Proof by Mathematical Induction:

Let P(n): ∑_{k=1}^{n} k² = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6

Base case (n = 1):
LHS = 1² = 1
RHS = 1(2)(3)/6 = 6/6 = 1 ✓

Inductive step: Assume P(m) is true for some positive integer m:
∑_{k=1}^{m} k² = m(m+1)(2m+1)/6

We must show P(m+1) is true:
∑_{k=1}^{m+1} k² = ∑_{k=1}^{m} k² + (m+1)²
= m(m+1)(2m+1)/6 + (m+1)²
= (m+1)[m(2m+1)/6 + (m+1)]
= (m+1)[m(2m+1) + 6(m+1)]/6
= (m+1)[2m² + m + 6m + 6]/6
= (m+1)[2m² + 7m + 6]/6
= (m+1)(m+2)(2m+3)/6

This is exactly the RHS of P(m+1). ✓

By the principle of mathematical induction, P(n) is true for all positive integers n. ∎

(i) the A.P.
(ii) the G.P.
(iii) the new sequence.
modelAnswer:
Let the AP have first term a and common difference d = 2: a, a+2, a+4, ...
Let the GP have first term b and common ratio r = 3: b, 3b, 9b, ...

New sequence: (a+b), (a+2+3b), (a+4+9b), ...

Given: 1st term = 8 → a + b = 8 ... (1)
Given: 3rd term = 52 → a + 4 + 9b = 52 → a + 9b = 48 ... (2)

Subtract (1) from (2): 8b = 40 → b = 5
From (1): a = 8 − 5 = 3

(i) The AP: first term = 3, d = 2 → 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, ...

(ii) The GP: first term = 5, r = 3 → 5, 15, 45, 135, ...

(iii) The new sequence (AP + GP term by term):
3+5, 5+15, 7+45, 9+135, ... = 8, 20, 52, 144, ...

question:
(a) A block of mass 3.5 kg rests on a rough plane which is inclined at an angle of 42° to the horizontal. If the coefficient of friction between the block and the plane is 0.75, what is the least force P parallel to the plane required to:
(i) start moving the block up the plane?
(ii) prevent the block from sliding down the plane? (Take g = 9.8 m/s²).
modelAnswer:
m = 3.5 kg, θ = 42°, μ = 0.75, g = 9.8 m/s²

Weight W = mg = 3.5 × 9.8 = 34.3 N
Normal reaction N = W cos θ = 34.3 cos 42° = 25.49 N
Friction force F = μN = 0.75 × 25.49 = 19.12 N
Component of weight along plane (down) = W sin θ = 34.3 sin 42° = 22.95 N

(i) Least force P to move block UP the plane:
Friction acts DOWN the plane (opposing upward motion).
P = W sinθ + F = 22.95 + 19.12 = 42.07 N ≈ 42.1 N

(ii) Least force P to prevent sliding DOWN:
Friction acts UP the plane (opposing downward tendency).
P + F = W sinθ
P = W sinθ − F = 22.95 − 19.12 = 3.83 N

modelAnswer:
H₀: The die is fair (each outcome equally likely).
H₁: The die is not fair.
α = 0.05

χ² = Σ(O − E)²/E

Outcome 1: (7−10)²/10 = 0.9
Outcome 2: (12−10)²/10 = 0.4
Outcome 3: (8−10)²/10 = 0.4

χ²_calc = 5.2

Degrees of freedom = 6 − 1 = 5
Critical value χ²_{0.05, 5} = 11.07

Since 5.2 < 11.07, we fail to reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence to conclude the die is unfair.

question:
(a) (i) Distinguish between type I and type II errors.
(ii) Past record shows that the mean score of year II Accountancy students in Business Statistics is 56% with a standard deviation of 7%. A random sample of 45 year II students of this department was tested and the mean score was 52%. Verify at α = 0.05 if the average score of the students in this course has changed.
modelAnswer:
(i) Type I Error (α): Rejecting the null hypothesis H₀ when it is actually true. Probability = α.

Type II Error (β): Failing to reject H₀ when it is actually false. Probability = β.

(ii) H₀: μ = 56%
H₁: μ ≠ 56% (two-tailed)
α = 0.05

σ = 7%, n = 45, x̄ = 52%, μ₀ = 56%

z = (x̄ − μ₀)/(σ/√n) = (52 − 56)/(7/√45) = −4/(7/6.708) = −4/1.0435 = −3.834
